text.p: The Australian June 10-year bond futures contract extended Wednesday's modest bounce from 92.180 during after hours trading, edging back over 92.250 resistance.
The contract ended SYCOM at 92.260 and up from its 92.210 pit close, but still stands well short of Tuesday's pre-budget 11-week 92.370 peak.
Analysts expect the contract to be held back at resistance at 92.280 as the huge rejection from the recent peak could see the market struggle to follow-through the after hours advance.
On the downside, and beyond 92.180, support is at 92.080/92.100 before an eventual retracement to 92.000.

The firmer tone in SYCOM was in response to the positive reaction in U.S. Treasuries following a 0.6 percent drop in April, although the rally was tempered ahead of next Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
A weakening U.S. dollar, which fell further against the yen in very late New York trading, also put a restraint on the advance. The April U.S. CPI is due later on Thursday.

Meanwhile, Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane is due to address a conference in Melbourne at 12.00 p.m. (0200 GMT) and the market will be keen to hear his response to Tuesday's budget, having proved to be a disappointment for the market.
